<description>
**Problem:** Addrman groups peer addresses by network prefix or (when ASMap finds a match) by autonomous system.
Without ASMap, grouping classifies the address twice.
With ASMap, an IP lookup allocates a temporary key and the decoder calculates a shift distance for each mantissa bit.
Building the group can also take several allocations for just a few bytes.

**Fix:** When ASMap is disabled, skip the extra address classification in `GetMappedAS`.
Build ASMap lookup keys on the stack and decode integers by shifting each bit into the mantissa.
Reserve space for the address group before appending its bytes.

**Time to group one IPv4 address:** (Raspberry Pi 5, ns per call, lower is better)

```text
                                 With ASMap                    Without ASMap
master      baseline             ███████████████████▉ 1,982    █████▏ 518
80a39cd417  Decode integers      ██████████████████▎  1,830    █████▎ 524
adc7012941  Skip empty map       ██████████████████▎  1,824    ███▉   390
bbe7b52765  Build lookup key     █████████████████▌   1,744    ████   394
13e0803197  Reserve group space  ████████████████▍    1,640    ███▏   307
```

Across the full series, `AddrManAdd` is 19.2% faster (59.1 to 49.6 ms).
</description>

<commits>
867b2a5bcb bench: measure ASMap validation and address groups

Time validation of the embedded ASMap. Measure `GetGroup` for the same IPv4 address with and without a map.
The existing lookup benchmarks cover `GetMappedAS` without constructing a group.

3feadee569 test: cover linked IPv4 lookup and ASN byte order

Use a single-prefix map with a four-byte ASN to cover the last ASN encoding class.
Truncating the offset in that class must invalidate the map.
Native IPv4 and its RFC 6052, RFC 6145, 6to4 and Teredo forms must resolve to the same ASN.

bc2caf6b86 util: simplify ASMap integer decoding

Skip classes with a set continuation bit, then shift in the bits of the offset within the selected class.
Keep returning `INVALID` for an empty class list before reading the selected class size.

On a Raspberry Pi 5 (GCC 13.3, Release), ASMapCheckStandard went from 42.65 to 39.29 ms (8.6% faster) and ASMapGetMappedASMulti went from 2266 to 2081 ns/address (8.9% faster).

6e05f35aaf net: return early from GetMappedAS without ASMap

Return before computing the network class when there is no map to search.

On a Raspberry Pi 5 (GCC 13.3, Release), ASMapGetGroupNoMap went from 523.82 to 389.93 ns/group (34.3% faster) and AddrManAdd went from 59.40 to 50.57 ms (17.5% faster). The grouping benchmark uses one IPv4 address.

24be384013 net: avoid temporary allocations in ASMap lookups

Build the lookup key on the stack. Use the computed network class to select the IPv4 encoding, and copy a native IPv6 address directly into the key.

On a Raspberry Pi 5 (GCC 13.3, Release), ASMapGetMappedASMulti went from 2091 to 1934 ns/address (8.1% faster).

4131eaa53f net: reserve space for the address group

Reserve room for the group tag and up to `ADDR_INTERNAL_SIZE` address bytes. This also covers the four-byte ASN of a mapped group.

On a Raspberry Pi 5 (GCC 13.3, Release), ASMapGetGroupMapped went from 1744.1 to 1639.8 ns/group (6.4% faster) and ASMapGetGroupNoMap went from 394.11 to 307.28 ns/group (28.3% faster). Both grouping benchmarks use one IPv4 address.
</commits>
